checked_sources.source: Le Yang, Vincent Y. F. Tan, Wang Chi Cheung, Best Arm Identification with Possibly Biased Offline Data, UAI 2025 / PMLR 286
checked_sources.result: Studies fixed-confidence best-arm identification with deliberately helpful, misleading, and partially biased offline data. Proves that without prior knowledge of a valid online/offline bias bound there is an impossibility tradeoff: improving over online-only on one instance can force worse sample complexity on another. LUCB-H uses auxiliary bias-corrected confidence bounds so historical samples contribute only when they can safely tighten bounds. Theorem 4.1 gives E[tau_delta] = O(sum_i (Delta_i^-2 log(1/delta) - Savu(i))) with Savu(i)=TS(i)*max(1-4 eta(i)/Delta_i,0); when historical data is misleading the saving term is zero and the bound is no worse than standard LUCB, while sufficiently compatible historical data can strictly reduce online samples. In 5-arm Gaussian experiments the authors deliberately set offline means so the offline phase identifies the wrong best arm; across variations in delta, offline sample size, and bias bound, LUCB-H behaves similarly to Pure LUCB in the misleading case, while beneficial histories require significantly fewer samples. At delta=0.01 its per-arm allocations in the misleading case are similar to Pure LUCB, whereas helpful arms can receive substantially fewer online samples.

checked_sources.source: Carl Hvarfner, Sam Daulton, Max Balandat, Eytan Bakshy, Pitfalls and Remedies for Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization, arXiv:2607.09073, 2026
checked_sources.result: Controlled transfer-BO audit on affinely related tasks finds that the textbook multi-task GP can attenuate or even flip recovered cross-task correlation and loses to a single-task GP on most base functions in the authors' multi-task BO grid despite the tasks being structurally easy to transfer between. Proposed remedies are explicit per-task mean/scale parameters, non-negative task covariance, and partial source-target co-location. These recover the target-only baseline on simple instances, but broader failure persists on harder instances and across most tested rank-based/latent-context variants. This is strong negative evidence against assuming that apparent task relatedness or standard MTGP correlation learning is itself a sufficient negative-transfer safeguard.

checked_sources.source: A. Tfaily et al., Transfer Learning in Bayesian Optimization for Aircraft Design, arXiv:2603.28999, 2026
checked_sources.result: The paper's tested TLBO examples beat vanilla BO in early convergence, including constrained aircraft design, but its negative-transfer section explicitly warns that highly dissimilar source/target landscapes can mislead the search. It proposes periodically alternating TLBO with target-only VBO to bound harm; however, adaptive detection/automatic selection between TLBO and VBO is stated as future work. Therefore this source supports the need for a target-only fallback but does not yet provide the requested same-experiment adaptive negative-transfer detector with a clean regret/frequency endpoint.

checked_sources.source: Alan Tan Wei Min, Abhishek Gupta, Yew-Soon Ong, Generalizing Transfer Bayesian Optimization to Source-Target Heterogeneity, IEEE TASE 18(4), 2021
checked_sources.result: Hetero-TBO learns a source-target coupling parameter lambda; at lambda=0 the source blocks have no influence on target prediction, giving an exact structural null-transfer limit. Theoretical analysis allows positive or negative correlation and the synthetic suite includes cases with differing source/target functions and dimensions. Across its six synthetic problems Hetero-TBO variants converge faster than conventional BO; on P2/P4 the function value reached by BO-EI at 40 evaluations is reached by Hetero-TBO-EI in under 30 (>25% evaluation saving). This supports learned source suppression, but the experiments are not an intentionally adversarial source-task stress test and therefore do not close the original negative-transfer frontier by themselves.

candidates_new.mechanism: Maintain an online/target-only evidence path as a correctness and sample-complexity shadow baseline, and allow historical/source evidence to tighten decisions only through confidence bounds that include an explicit, validated source-target bias allowance. Compute source usefulness per candidate/arm rather than globally. If the compatibility margin is too large relative to the decision gap, the historical-data saving term becomes zero and the procedure automatically falls back to online evidence for that candidate; if history is compatible, reuse it to reduce new samples.
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: Theorem 4.1 bounds expected online stopping time by the standard LUCB term minus Savu(i)=TS(i)*max(1-4 eta(i)/Delta_i,0). Thus sufficiently compatible historical data yields a positive sample saving, while misleading data yields Savu=0 and no asymptotic penalty relative to online-only LUCB under a valid bias bound. In deliberate 5-arm misleading-bias experiments where offline data points to the wrong best arm, LUCB-H tracks Pure LUCB in mean stopping time/error bars across confidence, offline-sample-size, and bias-bound sweeps; helpful-history runs require significantly fewer samples. At delta=0.01, misleading-history per-arm sampling is similar to Pure LUCB, while beneficial/partial cases selectively reduce samples on helpful arms.
candidates_new.operational_observable: For each reused evidence source and candidate, track a source-target discrepancy/bias bound V(i), current online confidence interval, historical confidence interval enlarged by V(i), decision gap Delta_i, and a computed historical saving/admissibility signal. Keep the target-only confidence path live. Historical evidence is allowed to reduce online evaluation only when its bias-adjusted interval can safely tighten the decision; otherwise ignore it for that candidate rather than globally trusting or globally discarding the source.
candidates_new.scope: Fixed-confidence best-arm identification with bounded online/offline distribution shift and a valid bias bound; Gaussian experiments plus theory under the paper's assumptions. It is not itself Bayesian optimization and does not prove that the same bound form transfers unchanged to arbitrary surrogate-based optimization.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: A valid bias bound is essential. The paper proves an impossibility tradeoff without prior knowledge of such a bound. Severe underestimation can cause over-trust of historical data, especially if the true best candidate is biased downward. Therefore the bias bound itself must be calibrated/conservative, and a target-only shadow baseline should remain available rather than being retired after early apparent source agreement.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Research-evaluation systems can reuse old benchmark runs, prior model generations, proxy experiments, or external studies without risking silent negative transfer by maintaining a live current-only decision path and admitting each historical evidence source only through an explicit compatibility/bias budget. This is a stronger guardrail than a single learned task-correlation scalar because it is candidate-local and has an explicit null-reuse limit.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source-domain theory/experiments; medium-high for research-evaluation transfer

evidence_updates.update: A newer controlled MTBO audit shows that standard learned cross-task correlation can fail even on perfectly affinely related tasks, including sign flips with multiple sources, and the textbook MTGP loses to target-only GP on most tested base functions. Therefore similarity estimation alone should not be treated as a sufficient safe-transfer gate; keep a target-only shadow and require an explicit admissibility/bias or held-out predictive check before source influence is allowed to dominate.

Nonstationarity and source bias now have distinct safeguards: changepoint/context alignment decides whether old evidence belongs to the current regime, while a bias-bounded shadow-baseline rule decides whether even same-regime historical evidence is safe enough to reduce current sampling.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: An automatic target-only fallback in transfer Bayesian optimization is already cleanly validated under deliberately misleading source tasks
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: The 2026 aircraft TLBO paper proposes alternating TLBO/VBO as a robustness device but states adaptive selection/detection as future work. Hetero-TBO has a structural lambda=0 null-transfer limit and tests different source/target functions, but not the requested deliberately adversarial source-task experiment with a clean negative-transfer frequency/regret endpoint.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Do not claim the exact transfer-BO frontier is closed. The stronger matched misleading-source evidence recovered in this run comes from best-arm identification, not BO.

frontier: Find transfer-BO primary work that intentionally injects adversarial/misleading sources and evaluates an actually implemented automatic target-only fallback or source-disable gate with clean regret/time-to-best/negative-transfer-frequency endpoints; compare against both naive transfer and target-only BO.

Find methods that learn or calibrate the source-target bias bound online while preserving a no-worse-than-target-only guarantee; this is the critical operational dependency exposed by LUCB-H's impossibility result when the bound is unknown or underestimated.

Find sequential wet-lab model-discrimination work with a random/uniform/nonadaptive DOE baseline and explicit experiments-to-identification numbers, including what happens when the true mechanism is outside the initial model set.

Quantify Bayesian optimization with common random numbers where the acquisition itself decides reuse-old-seed versus new-seed; extract exact evaluation/regret savings and failure regimes, then combine with the prior covariance-aware ranking result.
Find covariance-aware ranking/selection under jointly heavy-tailed or otherwise non-Gaussian correlated observations, ideally finite-budget, to unify correlation and tail guardrails.
